title: Constructible coefficient and Frobenius bridge for the Weil projection inputs
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $t$; put $A_n=R/(t^n)$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum], not a datum assuming projection invertibility. Schemes are finite type over $k$ and their structure morphisms need not be separated. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be its geometric base change. Use the Weil coefficient categories [def-wf-weil-category] and tensor [def-wf-tensor-product]. For $W=X,Y$ the integral constructible category underlying these conventions agrees, by the canonical completed coefficient identification, with the derived-complete constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] used by the operation datum. Its coefficient sheaf is $B_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ and its finite derived reductions and etale-origin witnesses are the same. For integral bounded constructible $M,N$ on $W$, the canonical comparison
$$\chi_W:M\otimes^L_{B_W}N\xrightarrow{\sim}M\widehat\otimes_R^LN$$
of [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion, def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] identifies the ordinary and completed tensor models. If the inputs have Weil maps, it satisfies $\chi_W\varphi_{\rm ord}=\varphi_{\rm comp}\Phi_W^*(\chi_W)$ for geometric Frobenius $\Phi_W$. These identifications persist after rationalization and common finite-field scalar extension. For $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,R)$, completed pullback, the two tensor expressions and the compact-support outputs in the projection formula stay bounded constructible in these identified categories. Thus the underlying operation outputs of rational or common-stage Weil inputs lie in precisely the coefficient domains required for [lem-fix-weil-operations], with its tensor Weil map identified with [def-wf-tensor-product]. Integral representatives are required only for the underlying objects, not for their rational Weil isomorphisms.

proof.text: Geometric base-change preserves separatedness, local finite type and quasi-compactness by Mathlib MorphismProperty.overPullbackMap. The completed coefficient comparison satisfies every quotient projection by its unique normalization. Finite type over the geometric field supplies Noetherianity and finite dimension; the coefficient-prime unit maps to global sections. Apply integralStratifiedPerfectDetailed to identify the integral predicates on the actual completed coefficient rings.

Apply WfTensorCompletion.integral to the pair. Its two membership clauses give the tensor domains. The full constructible inclusion reflects invertibility of the completion unit. Apply integral_equivariance for the specified integral Weil equation and wfTensorCompletionCommonField for the common-field isomorphism and its inclusion.

Take the normalized package and ordinary/completed Weil isomorphisms from wfTensorCompletionFrobenius_exists; no uniqueness is required. For the completed bifunctor, precompose its ambient inclusion with the product of the two raw localization functors. The normalized integral functor equality, the uniquely normalized constructible inclusion and the pure-tensor formula of wfRationalTensorHom give equality there. Curry, apply injectivity of precomposition with scalar localization, flip, and apply it again to get equality on arbitrary rational arrows. On each unchanged integral object, the completedMu normalization, inclusion normalization and wfRationalTensorPullback_exists identify the actual ambient Frobenius component. Every rational object is an unchanged integral object. For two arbitrary rational Weil maps, use the bifunctor equality on their tensor and the component equality, compose these heterogeneous equalities, and remove the identity transports in wfWeilStructure. This proves its displayed hom is exactly wfTensorFrobenius, including all denominators.

Scalar extension preserves the intrinsic integral predicate by sfIntegralScalarExtension_constructible. Apply the coefficient predicate equivalence at the target field to obtain the detailed coefficient-domain clause.

Choose P,H,U,V,B to be the actual restricted integral operation outputs of the datum. The integral pullback and tensor normalizations give their ambient object equations. The supportConstruction object normalization and sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor_obj identify U,V with the recorded compact-support values; sfQcqsCompactSupportRealization supplies their ambient proper/open isomorphisms. The normalized rational pullback and tensor object formulas and supportConstruction rational-value formula give all five rational output equalities.

Repeat the preceding argument for the coefficientStages G component, using its finite-level and integral normalization fields. The commonStageComparison supplies pullback and support isomorphisms. For tensors, finiteCoefficientCompositum G G = G, the stage-system unit identifies identity transitions, and commonStageTensorComparison followed by the rational tensor normalization identifies both common-stage tensors with inclusions of the integral outputs.

proof_origin.place: Weil-equivariance sentence; the remaining rational clause is assembled from normalized integral tensor and pullback components by localization precomposition injectivity and heterogeneous equality of composed ambient arrows.

No new nodes and no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply. The statement is unchanged. Step 1: lem-pur-rational-lattice-adic-domain (X and Y are separated finite-type geometric fibres) shows that I_E is the derived-complete integral category with the same sheaf and reductions, and def-wf-weil-category rationalizes exactly that category. Step 2: lem-wf-constructible-tensor-koszul-unit gives rho*chi^quot = eta, eta invertible, and both T and C(T) in C_E, which is the normalized chi_W. Step 3: lem-wf-tensor-completion-frobenius states the displayed Frobenius equation and its rational and common-field persistence, with the tensor Frobenius as in def-wf-tensor-product. Step 4: the pullback and tensor clauses of lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible, with L in D^b_ctf, a full subcategory of D^b_c by def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, together with lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible (field k, f separated of finite type, ell invertible), cover P, K⊗P, Rf_!K, Rf_!(K⊗P) and Rf_!K⊗L. These are the datum's operations by def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom and def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support. Step 5: raw rationalization keeps the objects and scalar extension preserves D^b_c, so the domain hypothesis of lem-fix-weil-operations holds for pullback, f_! and tensor only; internal Hom and f^! are not used. A cycle check over the snapshot finds no path from any dependency back to the item. There is no SGA citation, and the Mathlib searches are recorded honestly (one Loogle query unavailable). Small cases checked: empty scheme, f = id, the torsion representative R/t, and a rational Frobenius t^{-1} with no integral lattice. review_split's 'no such node' messages come from the tool not following the chapter symlinks. Advisories: the 4 off-unit tools in split_report.tool_uses are fine for the maintainer to record. Step 1 could have used the unit's own koszul-unit lemma for the category coincidence. The identification of lem-fix-weil-operations' 'canonical' tensor Weil structure with def-wf-tensor-product goes through the frobenius lemma's canonical mu-hat, which I accept. One hypothesis sentence in step 4 is misplaced, which is cosmetic.
